reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited paragraphs (14.8 Personnel) contain no non-solicit, no-hire or anti-inducement language — only supervision, assignment and subcontracting rights — so none of the NOSOLICIT detection triggers are present.

Absence of any restriction on the Customer matches the playbook's preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'), so no redline or counterparty comment is expected; the rendered redline is correctly identical to the original and no comment was proposed.

The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are inapplicable heuristics here — they presuppose an existing non-solicit clause to measure — and do not undermine the compliance conclusion.

Rationale is substantiated and appropriately scoped: it notes Section 14.16's freedom-to-contract language is not a covenant, and flags monitoring SOWs/orders with the fallback position if a restriction is reintroduced.
